why: "If this unit is riled up, this unit’s ranged attacks have [SUSTAINED HITS 1]" (Wahapedia and BSData read the same): being riled up is the only condition, with no phase or turn, so cond riled (the attacker's "Riled up") is right.

where: ooga-booga · Big Mek in Mega Armour
why: "This unit’s ranged attacks have: [IGNORES COVER]. If this unit is riled up, [SUSTAINED HITS 1]": the mark is on the [SUSTAINED HITS 1] bullet only, and "riled up" is that bullet's whole condition. [IGNORES COVER] needs nothing and has no mark.

"If this unit made a charge move this turn, this model’s melee attacks have +3 A, +2 S" (BSData has the same): making a charge move this turn is the whole condition, so cond charged is right. A Heroic Intervention charge also counts, because 15.11 has the unit "Resolve a charge", and the screen labels the Fight back switch that way.

"In your Shooting phase, if any of the following apply … This unit is within range of an objective. The target of that attack is within range of an objective": the situation is exactly "this unit or the target within range of an objective", and the objective fact is attacker OR target. The only other need is "your Shooting phase". The when names it, the ranged step is the attacker's own Shooting phase, and the code drops the tick for overwatch (/your shooting phase/).

where: Shoota Boyz rule · Dakka! Dakka! Dakka!
why: "Friendly ORKS INFANTRY units’ ranged attacks have: [ASSAULT]. While this unit is riled up, +3" R" (Wahapedia has the same wording): the mark is on the +3" bullet, whose only condition is being riled up. "This unit" can only mean the ORKS INFANTRY unit making the attacks, so the attacker's "Riled up" fact is right. The keyword need is handled by needs, not by cond.

"In your Shooting phase, when a friendly BREAKA BOYZ/FLASH GITZ/TANKBUSTAS unit is selected to shoot, if any of the following apply … That unit is within range of an objective. The target of that attack is within range of an objective": as with Finderz Keeperz, the situation is "this unit or the target on an objective". The other needs are "your Shooting phase" (in the when; overwatch is excluded by the code) and the unit keywords (needs).

where: ooga-booga · Big Mek in Mega Armour
why: "In the Fight phase, if this unit is riled up, this unit has +1 to hit rolls": the conditions are riled up plus the Fight phase. The mark is kind melee, and melee attacks are only made in the Fight phase (the Fight and Fight back steps, either turn), so cond riled ticks nothing the words exclude.

"ORKS model only. If this unit made a charge move this turn, this model’s melee attacks have +1 AP" (Wahapedia has the same): "ORKS model only" limits who can take the enhancement, not when it works, so the charge move this turn is the whole condition and cond charged is right.

"If this unit made a charge move this turn, this unit’s attacks have +1 D": a charge move this turn is the whole condition, so cond charged is right. The words say "attacks" and the mark says melee, but after a charge move in the same turn only melee attacks follow (shooting comes first, and a Heroic Intervention comes after overwatch). The screen also never applies charged to the Shoot step.

"If this unit made a charge move this turn, this unit’s melee attacks have +1 S" (the World Eaters faction pack's own change text is the same): a charge move this turn is the whole condition, so cond charged is right.

"Each time this model makes a Charge move, until the end of the turn, its hellforged weapons have the [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] ability" (BSData wording; Wahapedia says "melee weapons"): the effect holds for the rest of the turn once a charge move is made, which is exactly "made a charge move this turn", so cond charged is right.

"Each time this model makes a ranged attack that targets the closest eligible target within 18", you can re-roll the Hit roll" (Wahapedia has the same): the target being both the closest eligible target and within 18" is the whole condition, so cond closest18 is right. Its implication closest18 → closest is sound, and "closest" on its own does not tick this rule.

TARGET "One WORLD EATERS unit from your army that has not been selected to fight this phase and that made a charge move this turn", WHEN "Fight phase": the situation is "made a charge move this turn". The other needs are the keyword (needs), the Fight phase (phases) and not yet having fought, which holds for any unit about to fight. A stratagem is never ticked by a fact (it is only listed as "also the condition of 1CP Hack and Slash"), so nothing is over-ticked.

"If the attack targets a unit within range of an objective marker you do not control, you can re-roll the Wound roll instead": that is the whole condition of the full re-roll, which is marked cond targetObjectiveNotYours, while the re-roll of 1s is a separate always mod. Its implications (target on an objective marker → this unit or the target on an objective) follow from the words. One caveat on the label, not the mark: when the other side's list attacks, "you" in "you do not control" means the attacking player, not the viewer.

"Each time this model makes a ranged attack that targets a unit within range of one or more objective markers, that attack has the [IGNORES COVER] ability" (the Imperial Knights faction pack has the same): the target being in range of an objective marker is the whole condition, with no control requirement, so cond targetObjective is right. The core rules FAQ says an "objective marker" in a rule means an objective.

"Each time this model makes a ranged attack that targets the closest eligible target, add 1 to the Hit roll" (Wahapedia has the same): the target being the closest eligible target (01.04.02: closest to the model using the rule) is the whole condition, so cond closest is right.

"Each time this model makes a ranged attack that targets the closest eligible target, improve the Armour Penetration characteristic of that attack by 1" (Wahapedia has the same): the closest eligible target is the whole condition, so cond closest is right.

"In your Movement phase, if this model Remains Stationary, until the end of the turn, ranged weapons equipped by this model have the [SUSTAINED HITS 1] ability" (Wahapedia has the same): having remained stationary in your own Movement phase this turn is the whole condition, and that is the "Remained Stationary" fact (09.04: a move type selected in the Movement phase). The Shoot step is in the attacker's own turn, so the fact can only mean this turn's Movement phase.

"This unit’s ranged attacks that target the closest eligible target can re-roll hit rolls" (Wahapedia has the same): the closest eligible target is the whole condition of this effect, so cond closest is right. The charge part ("When this unit declares a charge …") is a separate effect, and the mark is not on it.
